facts.statement: Fukuititan is a sauropod dinosaur genus from the Early Cretaceous found in the Kitadani Formation in modern-day Japan.
facts.quote: Fukuititan (meaning "giant from Fukui prefecture") is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous (either Barremian or Aptian age) in the Kitadani Formation in what is now Japan.

facts.statement: Fukuititan fossils were discovered in summer 2007 at the Kitadani Dinosaur Quarry near the Sugiyama River by an expedition linked to the Fukui Prefectural Dinosaur Museum.
facts.quote: The fossils that would eventually be named Fukuititan were discovered in the summer of 2007 at the Kitadani Dinosaur Quarry, near the Sugiyama River, by an expedition in association with the Fukui Prefectural Dinosaur Museum

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Fukuititan, holotype FPDM-V8468, was described in 2010 by Japanese scientists Yoichi Azuma and Masateru Shibata.
facts.quote: The holotype and only specimen of Fukuititan, given the specimen number FPDM-V8468, was described in 2010 by Japanese scientists Yoichi Azuma and Masateru Shibata

facts.statement: Fukuititan is described as a medium-sized sauropod.
Subsequent authors have estimated Fukuititan to be 16.1 meters long, 5.75 meters tall at the shoulder, and weigh 5.75 tons.
facts.quote: subsequent authors have suggested a full length of 16.1 m long, a height of 5.75 m tall at the shoulder, and a mass of 5.75 t.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul suggested that the Fukuititan holotype represents an immature individual, meaning concrete adult size estimates may not be possible.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul later suggested that the holotype of Fukuititan represents an immature individual, and therefore no concrete estimates of its adult size can be made.

facts.statement: Fukuititan is distinguished from other titanosauriforms by stalk-like epipophyses on cervical vertebrae, a wide humerus, metacarpals half the length of the radius, and specific tooth features.
facts.quote: Fukuititan can be distinguished from all other titanosauriformes by the presence of a stalk-like epipophysis of the cervical vertebrae, a relatively wide humerus, metacarpals about half the length of the radius, and several features of the teeth.

facts.statement: Features of the tail vertebrae and fused ischia support classifying Fukuititan within Titanosauriformes.
facts.quote: Features of the caudal vertebrae and the co-ossification of the ischia lend support to its inclusion within Titanosauriformes.

facts.statement: Some phylogenetic analyses omit Fukuititan because its incomplete fossil record makes its classification unstable.
facts.quote: Some subsequent analyses have omitted Fukuititan from their phylogenetic analyses because its incomplete nature makes its placement unstable.

facts.statement: Fukuititan lived approximately 125 million years ago during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 125 millones de años, en el Aptiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Fukuititan lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Some sources describe Fukuititan as a relatively small sauropod with a total length of 10 meters.
facts.quote: Fukuititan es un sauropodo bastante pequeño con una longitud total de 10 metros.

facts.statement: Unique features of Fukuititan include an asymmetric dental crown with an absent or weak external groove and no internal cavity.
facts.quote: Las propiedades derivadas únicas, los autoapomorfismos , de este tipo son, una corona dental asimétrica extendida con un surco ausente o de forma débil en el exterior y sin un hueco en el interior.

facts.statement: Fukuititan cervical vertebrae have stalk-like epipophyses, the top width of the humerus is 32% of its length, and hand bones are 48% the length of the radius.
facts.quote: Las vértebras cervicales tienen epipofías en forma de tallo, el ancho de la parte superior del húmero es del 32% de la longitud de ese hueso; los huesos de las manos medias son largos con un 48% de la longitud del radio.

facts.statement: Fukuititan represents the first relatively complete titanosauriform skeleton found in Japan.
facts.quote: Representa el primer esqueleto relativamente completo de un titanosauriforme encontrado en Japón.

facts.statement: The Fukuititan holotype FPDM-V8468 is a partial skeleton found in Kitadani in 2006 and excavated from July 2007 to summer 2008.
facts.quote: El fósil holotipo, FPDM-V8468, consiste en un esqueleto parcial, encontrado en Kitadani en 2006 y excavado desde julio de 2007 hasta el verano de 2008

facts.statement: The preserved Fukuititan holotype includes a tooth, cervical vertebra, left scapula, left and right radius, humerus, right metacarpal, right femur and tibia, left fibula, sacral bones, and three tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: Se conservan, un diente, una vértebra cervical, un omóplato izquierdo, un radio izquierdo, un húmero y un radio derecho, una pierna media derecha, un fémur derecho, una tibia derecha, una pantorrilla izquierda, los huesos del sacro y tres vértebras de la cola.

facts.statement: Descriptors assigned Fukuititan to Titanosauriformes primarily because its tail vertebrae resemble those of the Asian species Borealosaurus.
facts.quote: Fukuititan ha sido asignado por los descriptores a los Titanosauriformes , principalmente debido a la forma de las vértebras de la cola que corresponde a la de la especie asiática Borealosaurus.

rejected.statement: Fukuititan's classification has varied over time, with D'Emic (2012) placing it in Macronaria, Mannion et al. (2013) in Titanosauriformes, and Sanz et al. (2014) in Somphospondyli.
rejected.quote: En 2012 D'Emic lo colocó en una más general Macronaria. Un año más tarde Mannion et al. volvió a considerarlo Titanosauriforme y en 2014 Sanz et al. lo encontró como Somphospondyli.
